name: Lazarus RipperDoc Street Clinic Full Kit
description:
The street ripperdoc's working uniform: a collarless surgical tunic in blood-resistant black neoprene, reinforced at the cuffs and chest with sealed syntex panels that wipe clean between procedures. Over it, a short open coat in pale graphite with deep external pockets sized for hand tools and neural probes. Integrated forearm channels allow the wearer's own chrome or aug hardware to operate unimpeded. Pants are flat-front, dark charcoal, with sealed inner-thigh pockets for sterile instrument pouches.

Footwear is a closed-toe clog in antimicrobial molded resin — easy to sanitize, slip-resistant on wet floors. A low filter hood with respirator snap-points completes the look. No branding. Bought in pieces, assembled by the doc herself.
functionality: Full fluid-resistance on tunic and coat, forearm aug channels for operating surgeons with chrome, sealed sterile pockets, slip-resistant footwear, respirator-compatible hood attachment points.
what_it_says: I fix what the licensed clinics won't touch, and I don't ask where you got the damage.
story_hooks: The doc's coat has a hidden inner pocket containing a folded corponation medical license — revoked, but laminated and kept.
A patient who died on the table left a data chip sewn into the lining; the doc hasn't looked at it yet.
CorpSec has started photographing anyone wearing this specific coat configuration in the Shelf district.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian medical silhouette with surgical precision. Collarless black neoprene tunic under a pale graphite open coat creates a stark, functional aesthetic. The overall impression is clinical efficiency—someone who moves fast between bodies and chrome. No decorative elements; every seam serves a purpose.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso for mobility, with compression panels at cuffs and chest for containment. Pants sit flat-front and straight-leg, allowing quick access to inner-thigh pockets. Coat hangs open and unbuttoned, creating an asymmetrical silhouette. Designed for someone operating in tight, bloody spaces.
physical_description.primary_material: Blood-resistant neoprene (tunic), sealed syntex reinforcement panels, pale graphite synthetic blend (coat), flat charcoal cotton-weave (pants), antimicrobial molded resin (clogs)
physical_description.texture: Smooth, wipeable neoprene with slight tackiness; syntex panels feel rigid and chemical-treated. Coat fabric has a dull matte finish. Resin clogs have subtle grip texturing on soles. Respirator hood fabric is tightly woven, moisture-resistant.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant blacks and charcoals with pale graphite accents. No pattern—solid utilitarian palette. Occasional staining from repeated sanitization is accepted wear.
physical_description.closures: Tunic: friction-fit; Coat: open, no closures; Pants: magnetic snap fly for speed; Clogs: slip-on; Hood: magnetic attachment points for respirator module
distinctive_features: Sealed syntex reinforcement at cuffs and chest—designed to contain bio-spillage
Integrated forearm channels routing along coat sleeves for chrome hardware visibility and operation
Deep external pockets in coat sized specifically for neural probes and micro-surgical hand tools
Sealed inner-thigh instrument pouches in pants—sterile, pressure-sealed
Low-profile filter hood with respirator snap-points (module sold separately)
Antimicrobial resin clogs with drainage channels molded into sole
Zero branding—intentionally unmarked to avoid corpo/legal identification
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 working-class street labor, with sub-grade (Tier 5) DIY assembly aesthetic. Not affordable to most, but assembled from scavenged/bootleg components—signals independence from supply chains.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street ripperdoc uniform. Wearing this signals illegal or semi-legal augmentation work, medical autonomy, and refusal of corpo medical licensing. Projects competence mixed with outlaw status. The wearer is someone who operates in the margins—trusted by those who can't access legal clinics.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately weathered. Faint stains around cuffs and chest from repeated sanitization cycles. Syntex panels show micro-scratches from tool contact. Clogs have scuff marks. The 'broken-in' look is earned—this is work gear, not display gear.
